  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  (Notice No. N2M25-52)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held
on Tuesday, May 6, 2025, commencing at 12:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California pursuant to the order of the
Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code, and
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

  MISSION STATEMENT

  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and
  quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive
  business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our
  community.

Watch and listen to the meeting as follows:

8656 and entering Webinar ID: 844 5272 9411 and Passcode: 281050. Please Note: All members of
the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed. If there are
technical difficulties with Zoom during the meeting, the meeting will proceed regardless. Meetings can
also be viewed via livestream here: https://www.spectrumstream.com/streaming/alhambra/live.cfm
Addressing the Council:
In person: Section 2.04.210 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishes the procedures for addressing
the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should complete a Speaker
Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you wish to speak. When called
upon by the presiding officer, please step to the podium.
Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise
Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.
Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the
maximum time to such period of time as the Council may determine.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Council who refuses to stop speaking after his/her
time has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the
progress of the City Council meeting who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such
behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers upon direction of the presiding officer.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, shall be Sergeant-at-Arms of the
Council meetings. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding
officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Council meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City official or their designees, shall be
permitted within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the express consent of the Council.

Agenda Tracking Numbers: All numbers listed in bold after the title of each Agenda item are City Clerk
tracking numbers that are used for filing and research purposes.

  ROLL CALL:  Maza, Maloney, Wang, Andrade-Stadler, Lee

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-52

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City
Council being held this afternoon pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

PRESENTATION

1.  BUDGET WORKSHOP – F2M25-17

  At the February 24, 2025 City Council Meeting, it was requested staff provide a Budget
  Workshop in addition to the June 23, 2025 Public Hearing to consider approval of the
  Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2025-26 through 2026-27, and Capital Improvement Plan
  for Fiscal Years 2025-2030. Topics to be discussed in the Budget Workshop include:
  Explanation of Budgetary Funds; Overview of the Fiscal Year 2025-26 and 2026-27
  Budget; Fiscal Year 2025-3030 Capital Improvement Plan; 5-Year Financial Forecast;
  Long-Term Liabilities; Reserve Fund Balances; Reserve Policy; Potential Federal
  Funding Impacts; Upcoming Fiscal Challenges; Review of 2025 Strategic Plan Priorities;
  Funding Estimates for Priorities; Economic Development Opportunities; and, 2025
  Strategic Plan Funding Recommendations. After the discussion, it is expected Council
  will provide direction to staff on funding recommendations for Fiscal Year 2025-26. Said
  requests will be included in the Draft Fiscal Year 2025-26 and 2026-27 Budget for
  consideration at the June 23, 2025 Council Meeting.

  Recommended Action:  City Council to provide direction to staff as deemed
  appropriate.

ADJOURNMENT

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.cityofalhambra.org and you
will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the

 Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Broadcast of Meeting: A live video stream of each Council meeting is available through the City’s
website. The regular meetings of the Alhambra City Council are recorded and are broadcast on
Charter Channels 3 and 182 at 7:30 p.m. on Thursdays and Mondays following the meeting.
Recordings are also available for viewing by the public on the City of Alhambra’s website, at the
Alhambra Public Library and, upon appointment, in the City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-
5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

Translation Services Requests: If you require translation services in order to participate in a
meeting please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 570-5090. All requests for translation services
shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting, staff will try to accommodate the
request if possible.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

  MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  May 6, 2025
  12:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 12:07 p.m. on Tuesday, May 6, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in Council
Chambers in Alhambra City Hall.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  ABSENT:  MAZA, MALONEY

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Director of Finance Lieu, Director
of Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of Police
Kennedy, Assistant Finance Director Tran, Manager Analyst Alvarez, Budget Analyst Pinto,

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-52

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this afternoon pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

PRESENTATION

1.  BUDGET WORKSHOP – F2M25-17

MAZA & MALONEY:  Councilmember Maza and Vice Mayor Maloney entered Council
Chambers at 12:08 p.m.

  At the February 24, 2025 City Council Meeting, it was requested staff provide a Budget
  Workshop in addition to the June 23, 2025 Public Hearing to consider approval of the Annual
  Budget for Fiscal Year 2025-26 through 2026-27, and Capital Improvement Plan for Fiscal
  Years 2025-2030. City Manager BINNQUIST and Director of Finance LIEU delivered a
  PowerPoint presentation, a copy of which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. Topics discussed
  in the Budget Workshop included: Explanation of Budgetary Funds; Overview of the Fiscal
  Year 2025-26 and 2026-27 Budget; Fiscal Year 2025-3030 Capital Improvement Plan; 5-Year
  Financial Forecast; Long-Term Liabilities; Reserve Fund Balances; Reserve Policy; Potential
  Federal Funding Impacts; Upcoming Fiscal Challenges; Review of 2025 Strategic Plan
  Priorities; Funding Estimates for Priorities; Economic Development Opportunities; and, 2025
  Strategic Plan Funding Recommendations. After the discussion, it was expected Council
  would provide direction to staff on funding recommendations for Fiscal Year 2025-26. Said
  requests would be included in the Draft Fiscal Year 2025-26 and 2026-27 Budget for
  consideration at the June 23, 2025 Council Meeting.

  City Manager BINNQUIST delivered an explanation of budgetary funds including unrestricted
  funds, special revenue funds – restricted funds, enterprise funds – restricted for specific uses,
  internal service funds. Director of Finance LIEU provided a budget overview and reviewed
  topics such as: All Funds Spending plan, proposed budget for all funds, proposed unassigned
  general fund budget overview, general fund revenue sources, sales and use tax industry
  groups, general fund expenditures, CAL PERS Rates, and the 5-year financial forecast.

  1
5-6-25
   Discussion: Mayor LEE, Ms. LIEU, and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the use of the Budget
  Surplus, the projection for the future of the Budget Surplus, and the use of the General Fund
  – Unrestricted Use for various projects including deferred maintenance projects.
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER, Ms. LIEU and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed various
  taxes such as the Measure AL tax and its specific uses as well as the proposed TOT tax ballot
  measure. They also discussed City departments which use restricted funds or restricted funds
  for specific use, such as Public Works and Utilities. Vice Mayor MALONEY and Ms. LIEU also
  discussed Special Revenue Funds. Councilmember WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST briefly
  discussed Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) which were funded and those that would be
  deferred at this time. Councilmember MAZA and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the uncertainty
  of federal funds at this time.

  Ms. Binnquist and Ms. Lieu continued the presentation. Ms. LIEU provided an overview of
  FY2025-2026 Capital Improvement Projects (CIP), Public Safety CIP, other CIP requests, the
  FY2026-2027 CIP Plan, and the FY 2026-2027 CIP Requests. Ms. BINNQUIST provided an
  overview and explanation of FY 2025-2026 and FY 2026-207 Position Changes for Full-Time
  Staff. Ms. LIEU continued with an explanation and overview of long-term liabilities, General
  Fund Reserve balance, and the General Fund Review history. Ms. BINNQUIST concluded
  this presentation with an explanation of Federal Grants and upcoming fiscal challenges
  anticipated by the City.

  Discussion: Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Director of Public Works and Utilities AHLEN
  discussed the unfunded mandate from the State of California for a Cross Connection
  Coordinator. Mr. AHLEN explained that the State required a full-time staff member to supervise
  the connection device to the potable water system for monitoring purposes.

  Ms. WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the City’s preparedness in the event of an
  economic recession. Ms. BINNQUIST stated that the City maintained and operated a
  conservative baseline budget and that any additions were based on necessity. She stated that
  the City insisted on grants whenever possible to alleviate the burden on the general fund. She
  discussed the additions to the general fund reserve and that the City continued to try to add
  money to it whenever possible. She stated that in the event of a recession, the City would not
  continue with unfunded projects. She also addressed concerns regarding staff and stated that
  the City would only hire necessary staff members based on expanding needs and Council
  priorities for programs. Ms. WANG supported staff’s practices and supported continuing to
  align reserves with long term liabilities. Ms. LEE emphasized the need to prioritize current staff
  positions and maintaining health benefits in the event of a recession.

  Ms. BINNQUIST delivered a presentation regarding the 2025 Strategic Plan funding estimates,
  a copy of which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. In addition to providing costs and funds for
  current projects, Ms. Binnquist highlighted items which were unfunded general fund items and
  requested Council consider providing input or recommendations on which items would receive
  funding from the budgeted amount of $1,300,000. Ms. BINNQUIST provided two corrections.
  Firstly, that Objective Number 2.16 be removed from consideration, as staff discovered that
  funding could be provided through Measure R funds. Secondly that Objective Number 3.9 did
  not have a ballot cost associated.

  Ms. BINNQUIST stated that given the time allocated for the special meeting, she suggested
  that Council was not required to provide recommendations at this time if they required more
  time. She stated that Council could review the provided worksheet and make
  recommendations during an agendized discussion at the next City Council meeting. She
  further clarified that should Council decide to not provide recommendation on any of the
  Strategic Planning Objectives at this time, that these unfunded items would not be included in
  the draft budget which would be presented at the June 23, 2025 regular City Council meeting;

  2
5-6-25
   but could be added through budget amendments at a later date. She added that if Council did
  not choose to move forward with funding allocation, then staff would be unable to begin
  working on the strategic plan items.

  Discussion:  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER supported moving forward with Objective 3.9.

  Mr. MALONEY suggested staff discuss future grant opportunities with Clean Power Alliance
  for Objective 1.2. He supported funding for Objective 2.9. He went on to suggest that Staff
  work with the Downtown Business Association regarding Objective 2.12. He stated that there
  was an opportunity to reevaluate operation of the downtown area as a model for Valley
  Boulevard. He suggested staff review the assessment district for the area and include
  provisions for maintenance of Main Street and the public parking structures. Mr. MALONEY
  further suggested seeking grants from outside entities for Objective 2.14. He discussed
  Objective 3.6 and suggested either staff or a Council Subcommittee first meet with the local
  business community and the Downtown Business Association to receive their input directly
  before hiring a consultant. Mr. MALONEY and Director of Community Development HO further
  discussed staff’s interpretation of the work required for Objective 3.6 and 6.5. Mr. MALONEY
  went on to discuss the East Main Corridor and the Central Business District up to Almansor
  Street. He stated that he continued to have reservations about hiring a consultant but added
  that he would support a consultant to pinpoint specific issues and properties for development,
  especially if there was less incentive to enact a vacant property tax.

  Mr. MAZA stated that he supported any measures for Police, Fire, and public education. He
  discussed the correlation between successful economic development and public safety. He
  stated that given the time allotted, he would reserve additional comment for another meeting.

  Ms. WANG stated that she would also reserve most of her comments and recommendations
  for the next meeting. She supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion for Objective 1.2 as a green
  initiative and discussed the public safety aspect. She suggested in the interim for a Street Light
  Master Plan, staff should address the most problematic areas from the master plan. She
  suggested allocating funding and resources to prioritize problem areas to ensure safety. Ms.
  WANG went on to discuss Objective 2.14 and added that being proactive in structure updates
  would save money as opposed to more expensive damage in the event of an earthquake. She
  stated that under the Hazard Mitigation Plan, the City could also look to federal funding and
  grant opportunities in the future. Ms. WANG also supported Mr. Maloney’s comments
  regarding Objective 3.6 and supported meeting with the business community and use the
  partnership with the Chamber of Commerce to discuss their issues and concerns. She
  supported more in-depth conversations regarding Objective 3.9 in the future.

  Ms. LEE discussed Objective 2.12 and expressed support for allocating funds for street
  washing. She added that she would prefer monthly washing in the downtown area. She stated
  that she would continue to review the recommendation worksheet and would provide further
  recommendations at a later date.

  Action Taken:  City Council reviewed and discussed presentation. No action was taken.

ADJOURNMENT:  At 1:56 p.m., Mayor LEE adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
  by
  BRIANNA LAMB MCCARTHY
  ASSISTANT CITY CLERK
